messages.subject: Monte Carlo study SEM lavaan: comparing estimates
parts:
Hello, I run a moderated mediation with a skewed moderator. 
I asked a question on SEMNET about the reliability of the results of the moderated mediation and they suggested me this procedure: 

"[...] you could run a Monte Carlo study with skewed moderator indicators analogous to your empirical data. Then you can find out whether the skewness of the moderator is problematic or not."

I would like to have a feedback on my understanding of the problem solution suggested.

Could you confirm that the boostrap procedure below is correct? I tried this:
  
x is the predictor, m the mediator, w is the moderator, w*m is the interaction. These are all latent variables. w*m is created using indProd function from semTools, and it is double-mean centered. The variance is fixed as default (i.e., first indicators)

model <- "
X=~  ... + ... + ... 
Y=~  ... + ... + ... 
W =~ ... + ... + ...
M=~  ... + ... + ...
W.M =~ ... + ... + ...

Y ~  a1*X + b*M + q*W + z*W.M
M ~ a*X

az:= a*z                              # IMM
ab :=  a*b                           # W==0
ab_1 := a * (b +  (-1 * z))  # W== -1
ab_2 :=  a * (b +  (1 * z))  # W== +1
"

#initialise bootstrap estimate vectors
estimates_IMM <- c()
estimates_SDless <- c()
estimates_SDzero <- c()
estimates_SDplus <- c()

set.seed(776699)
for (i in 1:1000) {
  #sample raw data with replacement
  df_temp<-df %>%
    sample_n(n(), replace = TRUE) 
  
  #fit model and extract estimates
  fit <- sem(model, data=df_temp, estimator="MLR")
  stand_solu<-standardizedsolution(fit)
  
  # save estimates
  estimates_IMM%<>%
    c(stand_solu$est.std[which(stand_solu$lhs == "az")])
  
  estimates_SDzero%<>%
    c(stand_solu$est.std[which(stand_solu$lhs == "ab")])
  
  estimates_SDless%<>%
    c(stand_solu$est.std[which(stand_solu$lhs == "ab_1")])
  
  estimates_SDplus%<>%
    c(stand_solu$est.std[which(stand_solu$lhs == "ab_2")])
  
}

# fit model on raw data to get rank of estimates for 
# Holm's correction when computing confidence intervals below

fit <- sem(model, data=df, estimator="MLR") #here is using the real data

real_stand_solu<-standardizedsolution(fit) %>%
  filter(lhs %in% c("az", "ab", "ab_1", "ab_2")) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(est.std)))

real_stand_solu

#compute corrected bootstrap confidence interval
ci_SDplus<-quantile(estimates_SDplus, probs = c(.05/2/4, 1-(.05/2/4)))
ci_az<-quantile(estimates_az, probs = c(.05/2/3, 1-(.05/2/3)))
ci_SDzero<-quantile(estimates_SDzero, probs = c(.05/2/2, 1-(.05/2/2)))
ci_SDless<-quantile(estimates_SDless, probs = c(.05/2/1, 1-(.05/2/1)))

Then, I establish if my data with the skewed moderator is problematic or not by comparing results from the boostrapped estimates and the estimates from the real data?

Thank you very much for any help you could provide.

messages.subject: Re: Monte Carlo study SEM lavaan: comparing estimates
parts: you could run a Monte Carlo study with skewed moderator indicators analogous to your empirical data
Could you confirm that the boostrap procedure below is correct?

They did not suggest bootstrapping.  They suggested generating random data that resembles your data, not resampling from your original data.  

From what I have read, skewed predictors are only problematic with residual-centered product-indicators, not double-mean-centered product-indicators.  But you will want to estimate the factor correlations if you can be sure of normality.

https://doi.org/10.3390/psych3030024  (see Section 1.3)

Terrence D. Jorgensen
